'''Hendrika Cornelia Scott (Henda) Swart''' <small>[[Royal Society of South Africa|FRSSAf]]</small> (born 1939, died February 2016 [age 77-78])<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.royalsocietysa.org.za/?page_id=759 |title=Fellows (FRSSAf) |date=December 2016 |website=Royal Society of South Africa |access-date=2017-11-29 |archive-date=2018-09-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180905155258/http://www.royalsocietysa.org.za/?page_id=759 |url-status=dead }}</ref> was a South African mathematician, a professor emeritus of mathematics at the [[University of KwaZulu-Natal]] and a professor at the [[University of Cape Town]]<ref name="rssa">[http://www.royalsocietysa.org.za/wp-content/uploads/2013/01/HendaSwart.pdf Fellow citation] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200207031529/http://www.royalsocietysa.org.za/wp-content/uploads/2013/01/HendaSwart.pdf |date=2020-02-07  }}, [[Royal Society of South Africa]], 1996, retrieved 2015-01-17.</ref><ref name="marching">{{citation|title=Women Marching Into the 21st Century: Wathint' Abafazi, Wathint' Imbokodo|author=Group Democracy and Governance, Human Sciences Research Council|publisher=HSRC Press|year=2000|isbn=9780796919663|contribution=Swart, Henda|pages=192–193|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YgzGqNhLY1UC&pg=PA192}}.</ref>

== Personal life ==
Born Hendrika Cornelia Scott, she married John Henry Swart.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Swart.html|title=Hendrika Swart (1939-2016)|website=www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref> They had three children Christine, Sandra and Gustav.<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
Swart began teaching at the University of Natal in 1962.<ref name="marching"/> She was the first person to earn a doctorate in mathematics from [[Stellenbosch University]],<ref name="marching"/> in 1971, with a dissertation on the geometry of [[projective plane]]s supervised by Kurt-Rüdiger Kannenberg.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=72354}}</ref> In 1977, her research interests shifted from geometry to [[graph theory]], which she continued to publish in for the rest of her career.<ref name="marching"/>

She was the editor-in-chief of the journal ''Utilitas Mathematica'',<ref name="rssa"/><ref name="marching"/><ref>[http://bkocay.cs.umanitoba.ca/utilitas/index.html ''Utilitas Mathematica'' home page] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150127063355/http://bkocay.cs.umanitoba.ca/utilitas/index.html |date=2015-01-27 }}, retrieved 2015-01-17.</ref> and was vice president of the [[Institute of Combinatorics and its Applications]].<ref name="rssa"/><ref name="marching"/> In 1996 she became a [[fellow]] of the [[Royal Society of South Africa]].<ref name="rssa"/>

Swart was a part-time lecturer at the University of Cape town from 2014 until her death.<ref name=":0" />

== Publications ==
She published under the name Henda C Swart.<ref name=":0" /> She published nearly 100 papers from 1980 to 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/Extras/Swart_publications.html|title=Swart publications|website=www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref>

== Research ==

Swart began her research career in projective geometry, completing her doctoral thesis on Desarguesian planes at Stellenbosch University. During a sabbatical at the University of New Mexico in the late 1970s, she developed an interest in graph theory after attending lectures by Roger C. Entringer. This marked a change in her research direction, and graph theory became the principal focus of her work for the remainder of her career.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Hendrika Cornelia Scott Swart
 |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Swart/
 |website=MacTutor History of Mathematics
 |publisher=University of St Andrews
 |access-date=14 July 2026
}}</ref>

== Contributions ==

Swart's research covered several areas of graph theory, including graph vulnerability, distance-related graph parameters and domination theory. She also introduced undergraduate and postgraduate courses in graph theory, design theory, geometry and information security at the University of Natal, helping to establish graph theory as an active research area in South Africa.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Hendrika Cornelia Scott Swart
 |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Swart/
 |website=MacTutor History of Mathematics
 |publisher=University of St Andrews
 |access-date=14 July 2026
}}</ref>

== Mentorship ==

Throughout her career, Swart supervised more than twenty master's and doctoral students. Several of her former students later became academics and researchers, and she was widely recognised for encouraging young mathematicians to pursue research careers in graph theory.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Hendrika Cornelia Scott Swart
 |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Swart/
 |website=MacTutor History of Mathematics
 |publisher=University of St Andrews
 |access-date=14 July 2026
}}</ref>

== Professional service ==

Swart served as Editor-in-Chief of ''Utilitas Mathematica'' and as Vice-President of the Institute of Combinatorics and its Applications. She also served on the Committee of the African Mathematical Union and represented South Africa in international mathematical organisations.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Hendrika Cornelia Scott Swart
 |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Swart/
 |website=MacTutor History of Mathematics
 |publisher=University of St Andrews
 |access-date=14 July 2026
}}</ref>

== Honours ==

Swart was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society of South Africa in 1996 in recognition of her contributions to graph theory, mathematics education and research leadership. She later became Professor Emerita at the University of KwaZulu-Natal.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Hendrika Cornelia Scott Swart
 |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Swart/
 |website=MacTutor History of Mathematics
 |publisher=University of St Andrews
 |access-date=14 July 2026
}}</ref>
